book_concept.purpose: A teaching book that shows believers what they already inherited in Christ — resurrection life, union with the Father, unconditional love and usable spiritual authority — and how to practice it daily.
book_concept.core_subject: A multi-session teaching corpus expounding Hebrews 2, John 17, Colossians 3, Malachi and related texts, joined to personal testimony of healing, resurrection and providence.
book_concept.reader_journey: From inherited habit, tradition and fear of death, through scriptural exposition of destroyed death and granted union, into a disciplined practice of mind, prayer and ministry, ending in testimony and prophetic vision.
book_concept.editorial_progression: Diagnosis of inherited religion → doctrinal foundation (resurrection life, offices, union) → interior anatomy and mental discipline → practice and testimony → corporate vision.

title_candidates.title: Flesh and Bone
title_candidates.rationale: Anchors the central corrective about physical resurrection and real inheritance.

title_candidates.title: Already Yours
title_candidates.rationale: Captures the recurring claim that life, love, power and grace are already given.

title_candidates.title: One With the Father
title_candidates.rationale: Foregrounds the John 17 spine of the corpus.

subtitle: Resurrection life, union with God, and the practice of spiritual authority
editorial_angle: Treat the corpus as a sustained correction: against legalism, rapture-fixation, performance ministry and fear of death, replaced by inheritance already granted and practiced.
target_reader: Local congregations, retreat attendees, pastors and ministers receiving in-person Bible teaching and testimony.
editorial_strategy: Group the scattered sessions by doctrinal and practical theme rather than chronology; place exposition before interior discipline, discipline before testimony, and reserve testimony chapters as demonstration of the earlier teaching. Uncertainties are flagged in situ, never resolved.

chapters.purpose: Open with the diagnosis: inherited custom and secondhand information replacing direct hearing from God.
chapters.summary: Direct hearing, bodily discipline, cultural food habits, tradition versus faith, ambition for long life.

sections.purpose: Establish the governing complaint about reliance on external information.
Use retreat discipline and food custom as the concrete entry point.
State the doctrinal principle that only Christ is accepted, not custom or condition.
Introduce longevity and the tree of life as an unresolved ambition that frames the book.

editorial_actions.note: Cluster the retreat-opening practical material with the tradition-versus-faith argument it serves.

chapters.working_title: Flesh and Bone: The Resurrection You Inherit
chapters.purpose: Lay the central doctrinal correction about physical resurrection and restored sonship.
chapters.summary: Flesh and bone inheritance, sons of men becoming sons of God, Adam's failure and Christ's intercession, life already possessed.

sections.working_title: Spirits Have No Flesh and Bone
sections.purpose: Present the corrective against die-well preaching and positional-only readings.

sections.working_title: From Sons of Men to Sons of God
sections.purpose: Trace the fall of sonship and its restoration in Christ.

sections.working_title: The Silence of Adam, the Prayer of Christ
sections.purpose: Contrast Adam's failure to intercede with Christ's intercession for the church.
Close the doctrinal claim: eternal life already possessed, persecution notwithstanding.

editorial_actions.note: Doctrine of resurrection placed before the Hebrews 2 session that argues for it.

chapters.purpose: Work the group exposition of Hebrews 2 and its consequences for preaching and fear.
chapters.summary: Live reading of Hebrews 2, translation dispute, African demonic emphasis, power already indwelling, accountability for the gospel preached.

sections.purpose: Carry the group reading and the contested rendering without resolving it.

sections.working_title: The Devil Men Still Boast Of
sections.purpose: Address the contrast between global and African experience of the demonic.
Move from spectator admiration of a powerful Christ to participation.
Turn the exposition into ministerial accountability and new boldness in prayer.

editorial_actions.note: Separate the text exposition from the cultural-context discussion it provoked.

chapters.purpose: Set out the sacred offices, the ordered priesthood, and the warnings attached to it.
chapters.summary: Shadow and fulfillment, three offices, universal versus ordered priesthood, Melchizedek, Malachi's warning, not despising the calling.

sections.purpose: Frame Old Testament encounter as prefiguration.
Define the offices and the distinction between common and ordered priesthood.
Use Melchizedek to teach discernment of spiritual authority.
Carry the covenant of life and peace and the curse on an unguarded blessing.

sections.working_title: Let No One Despise the Calling
sections.purpose: Correct false modesty and strain for recognition among ministers.

editorial_actions.note: Consolidate all office/authority material scattered across sessions.

chapters.purpose: Dismantle condition-based access to God: anointing, offering, worship, fasting.
chapters.summary: Activating the anointing, heart behind sacrifice, worship as fellowship, simplicity of receiving power, purpose and limits of fasting.

sections.purpose: Distinguish possessing a blessing from accessing it.
Present heart attitude as decisive for sacrifice.
Separate performative expression from genuine encounter.

sections.working_title: Nothing Added to What He Said
sections.purpose: Attack manufactured suffering doctrines and formulas for power.
Give fasting its real profit without making it a condition or a method.

editorial_actions.note: Link the fasting critique back to the tradition-versus-faith argument of Chapter 1.

chapters.purpose: Make John 17 the structural spine: union, glory, preservation, and the critique of rapture-centered focus.
chapters.summary: Jesus' prayer, sanctification, unity and glory, honesty about one's stand, rapture critique, overflow of communion, the Holy Spirit as person, the promised dimension, sensitivity to spiritual levels.

sections.purpose: Present Jesus' union with the Father and his prayer for preservation and sanctification.
Expound unity of essence and glory given to believers.

sections.working_title: Be Factual About Where You Stand
sections.purpose: Correct exaggerated faith declarations and account for stages of growth.
Deliver the critique of rapture-centered eschatology and its passivity.
Contrast rehearsed formulas with authority flowing from communion.

sections.working_title: Knowing the Spirit, Not Only the Gifts
sections.purpose: Shift emphasis from isolated gifts to relationship and vessel-cooperation.
Carry the promised dimension where the supernatural feels natural, and the simple confession it yields.
Balance bold authority with pastoral sensitivity to differing spiritual levels.

editorial_actions.note: Gather all John 17 material from separate sessions into one chapter.
Place the rapture critique inside the John 17 chapter as its direct corollary.

chapters.working_title: Loved Exactly as Jesus Is Loved
chapters.purpose: Hold the unconditional love text against conditions preachers add, then show God's use of flawed people.
chapters.summary: John 17:23 on divine love, illegitimate conditions, goodness producing purity, imperfect biblical figures carrying great power.

sections.purpose: Expound the love claim and the transformation it produces.
Assemble the biblical cases of imperfect figures carrying power.

editorial_actions.note: Tie unconditional love directly to the flawed-vessel argument.

chapters.purpose: Move from doctrine to the first practical discipline: fixing the mind on heavenly reality.
chapters.summary: Colossians 3 practice, Philippians 4:8 in ordinary life, mind as battlefield, completeness under the Head.

sections.purpose: Give the nightly, deliberate practice of conscious fellowship and anchored focus.
Apply Philippians 4:8 to ordinary movement and establish the mind as battlefield.
Argue the contradiction between a powerful Head and a sick, poor body.

editorial_actions.note: Begin the practice half of the book with the mind discipline.

chapters.purpose: Expose self-imposed legalism from imitation and recover personal uniqueness before God.
chapters.summary: Imitation-born rules, individuality of spiritual experience, God's intimate knowledge, long process behind testimonies, historical cost of discipleship and coerced religion.

sections.purpose: Show how imitation of a model creates private legalism.

sections.working_title: He Knows How He Made You
sections.purpose: Affirm deliberate individual making and the long process behind breakthrough.

sections.working_title: The Real Cost of the Doctrine
sections.purpose: Restore the occupied, coercive context of Jesus' teaching and of church history.

editorial_actions.note: Join the self-imposed-law teaching with the historical-cost material that corrects easy modern readings.

chapters.purpose: Give the anatomy that the practice chapters depend on.
chapters.summary: Tripartite man, conscience, soul as hub, the dying that began at the Fall, growth into sonship, the devil's nature and contested identifications.

sections.purpose: Define spirit, soul and body and the soul's channeling function.
Present the Fall as progressive spiritual decay and the growth back into sonship.
Carry the asserted distinction between Lucifer, Satan and the devil without resolving it.
Locate the development work in the soul, not the already-complete spirit.

editorial_actions.note: Separate structural anatomy from the Fall narrative and from the Lucifer/devil distinction.

chapters.purpose: Distinguish natural knowledge from revelation and define the believer's real combat.
chapters.summary: Simplicity in Christ, flesh-and-blood knowledge, relevance to one's society, pastoral discernment in miracle settings, weapons and captive thoughts.

sections.working_title: The Simplicity That Is in Christ
sections.purpose: Warn against deception away from simplicity and model meekness with authority.
Distinguish revelation from natural knowledge while demanding relevance.
Insist on physical care and discernment alongside spiritual acts.
Define the combat as reasonings and insist on guarding the barrier of the mind.

editorial_actions.note: Carry the mind-as-battlefield claim from Chapter 8 into explicit warfare terms.

chapters.purpose: Reform prayer practice: tongues rightly used, correction received, hunger as the condition.
chapters.summary: Misused tongues, refreshment through tongues, the speaker's correction, sincerity without knowledge, hunger and thirst as anchor.

sections.purpose: Expose all-night undiscerning tongues and unpracticed instruction.
Present the stated primary benefit of tongues and its short practical use.

sections.working_title: He Told Me I Was Tired
sections.purpose: Carry the personal correction and the need to adjust sincere but mistaken practice.
Establish hunger as the anchor condition for receiving more.

editorial_actions.note: Collect prayer/tongues material scattered across several sessions.

chapters.working_title: The Renewed Mind and the Hidden Faculty
chapters.purpose: Teach renewal of the mind and imagination as the method of lasting communion.
chapters.summary: Living sacrifice through renewal, the brain as instrument, imagination as God-given faculty, bringing Jesus into thought, trained meditation.

sections.purpose: Locate renewal in deliberate thought rather than power or spirit alone.

sections.working_title: The Power the Church Did Not Teach
sections.purpose: Present imagination as a neglected God-given faculty and compare other traditions' use of it.
Apply imagination to prayer so mind and spirit agree.
Give the habits of compartmentalizing, pre-sleep focus and graduated growth.

editorial_actions.note: Separate the faculty teaching from its prayer application and from meditation habits.

chapters.purpose: Move into the exercise of power: abnormal faith, short prayer, hands, holiness, effortless gifts.
chapters.summary: Abnormal acts and short prayers, humility about untested doctrine, hands as doorways, holiness and simple faith, gifts flowing without struggle.

sections.purpose: Teach the short confident prayer and acting without knowing the outcome.
Carry the torn-veil teaching and the two corroborating visions.
Connect inner purity to unobstructed authority and simple faith for healing.
Describe mature operation of the gifts as overflow rather than effort.

editorial_actions.note: Join the practice of faith with the teaching on hands, holiness and gifts.

chapters.purpose: Show how much is already given and how believers testify to discovering it.
chapters.summary: Grace exceeding imagination, Moses contrasted with indwelling, retreat testimonies, healing already accomplished, progressive understanding, the sower as stages of one life.

sections.purpose: Expound grace and truth through Jesus against law through Moses.
Carry participants' testimonies of shifted worship and renewed strength.
State healing as finished and understanding as dimensional.
Read the parable as stages of growth and charge the shepherd to keep sowing.

editorial_actions.note: Place firsthand testimonies immediately after the grace teaching they illustrate.

chapters.purpose: Resolve the fear-of-death thread opened in the resurrection chapters.
chapters.summary: No fear of death, fear as the devil's old strategy, death as gain lived rather than recited, peaceful departures.

sections.purpose: Convert the doctrine of destroyed death into lived attitude.

editorial_actions.note: Close the loop with Hebrews 2 on bondage through fear of death.

chapters.purpose: Make intentionality the organizing practice: speech, protection, and the responsibility of choice.
chapters.summary: Deliberate daily practice, aura of protection, speech correction, poverty as choice not design, balancing warning and promise.

sections.purpose: Establish deliberate daily practice, self-monitoring speech, and trust that protects.

sections.working_title: God Did Not Make Anyone Poor
sections.purpose: Work the disputed Proverbs reading and the role of choices and inherited patterns.

sections.working_title: The A Part and the B Part
sections.purpose: Balance warning passages with the promise of life in Christ.

editorial_actions.note: Attach the poverty-and-choice exposition to the intentional-living teaching.

chapters.purpose: Demonstrate the doctrine through resurrection accounts and the humility that must accompany them.
chapters.summary: The buried girl raised, activation of what God ordained, the young man raised, a prayer that did not succeed, the vessel's role.

sections.working_title: The Word That Could Not Fail
sections.purpose: Carry the prophecy tested by burial and the short prayer at the grave.
Frame miracle as releasing what is already ordained and direct the word rightly.
Hold the raised young man beside the woman who died, without softening either.
Keep results with God rather than with ministerial reputation.

editorial_actions.note: Place testimony after doctrine and practice so it functions as demonstration.

chapters.purpose: End with providence that reverses harm and the prophetic vision for the nation.
chapters.summary: Stolen Bible turned redemptive, loss treated as seed, declared exponential growth, vision of a transformed nation and a call to pray together.

sections.purpose: Carry the providence testimony and the seed-not-bitterness response to loss.
Close with the prophetic declaration, the national vision, and the call to pray together.

editorial_actions.note: Close the book with corporate vision following personal testimony.

uncertainty_handling.policy: UNC refs remain visible. The planner must not convert uncertainty into certainty. Unassigned UNC refs are listed, never erased.
